methodological_rigor.justification: This is a secondary long-term analysis of a well-conducted multicenter phase 3 RCT (SWOG S0016, NCT00006721) with 531 eligible patients analyzed in a modified intent-to-treat framework and a median follow-up of 15.5 years. Statistical methods are state-of-the-art for the question: Kaplan-Meier for OS/PFS, Aalen-Johansen competing-risk estimators, Gray test and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards, and a log-normal parametric mixture cure model selected by AIC with relative-survival framing against US life tables. Rigor is reinforced by sensitivity analyses (hypothetical missed progressions beyond 10 years; a flexible spline-based nonmixture relative cure model) and multivariable Cox adjustment for prognostic factors. Minor limitations are forthrightly acknowledged (imaging only required for 7 years; no central relapse pathology/imaging review; cohort predominantly non-Hispanic White); no formal power calculation for cure estimates is reported, but the analysis is secondary and CIs are provided throughout.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The underlying design is an individual randomized controlled trial with extended follow-up (SWOG S0016), supporting an Oxford LoE of 1b. The findings are highly clinically relevant: they directly challenge the dogma that advanced-stage FL is incurable by demonstrating a 42% model-based cure fraction and a plateau in relapse hazard, with concrete implications for patient counseling, de-escalation of indefinite oncology follow-up (transition to primary care after 10 years), and benchmarking of novel first-line agents. Endpoints are patient-relevant (OS, PFS, cumulative incidence of lymphoma-related death, second cancers), and prognostic stratification by FLIPI and beta-2 microglobulin provides actionable risk-adapted counseling. The paradigm-shifting nature of the conclusion, built on a mature randomized dataset, warrants the top relevance score.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT applies because the paper reports long-term outcomes of a randomized controlled trial, and the authors explicitly state the trial followed CONSORT. Key items are satisfied: ClinicalTrials.gov registration (NCT00006721), randomization scheme, intervention regimens with doses and schedules, eligibility criteria, primary and secondary endpoints, patient-flow via eFigure 1, adverse-event reporting (second cancers, AML/MDS, causes of death with eTables), and competing-risk accounting. Minor omissions include detail on allocation concealment, blinding (not specified for this follow-up analysis), and whether the long-term outcomes were pre-specified in the original protocol or added post hoc. No explicit data- or code-sharing statement is apparent in the blinded manuscript; the trial protocol is referenced in Supplement 1 but underlying patient-level data and analytic code (R flexsurvcure, SAS) are not indicated as publicly available.

novelty_literature.justification: The main novelty is empirical and conceptual: this is to the authors' knowledge the longest prospective follow-up (median 15.5 years) of a modern-era frontline chemoimmunotherapy randomized trial in advanced FL, and it applies formal relative-survival mixture cure modeling to argue a 42% cure fraction, directly challenging the long-standing incurability paradigm. The individual components (cure modeling, S0016 cohort, FLIPI/beta-2M prognostication) are not themselves new, and the manuscript appropriately situates itself relative to FOLL05, PRIMA, GALLIUM, StiL NHL1, and JCOG0203 (Watanabe et al., 15-year, no cure model). The combination of mature randomized follow-up with a rigorous relative-survival cure framework in FL fills a documented gap, but incremental cure-modeling applications in hematologic malignancies and prior Stanford/MDACC plateau observations prevent a top novelty score.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and well organized, with introduction, methods, results, and discussion each serving their proper purpose, and acronyms expanded on first use (FL, R-CHOP, CHOP-RIT, FLIPI, beta-2M). The abstract is unconventional in that it blends a question/answer format with structured sections, resulting in some redundancy and a slightly awkward opening, but it is quantitatively grounded and accurately mirrors the paper. Figure captions for Figures 1–3 are informative and standalone-interpretable, aligning numerically with the text (e.g., annual progression rates 6.8%/2.3%/1.1%/0.6%). Minor issues include a small typographical error in a confidence-interval label ("31% CI" for high FLIPI) and some repetition between results and discussion about the paradigm shift.

key_strengths: Mature 15.5-year follow-up of a randomized phase 3 trial (SWOG S0016, n=531) with 50% of living patients beyond 15 years
Rigorous relative-survival mixture cure modeling with AIC-based model selection, multiple sensitivity analyses, and a spline-based nonmixture alternative
Clinically paradigm-shifting conclusion: 42% estimated cure rate challenges FL incurability dogma, with concrete counseling and follow-up implications
Appropriate competing-risk framework (Aalen-Johansen, Fine-Gray) and multivariable prognostic analyses stratified by FLIPI and beta-2 microglobulin
Transparent reporting of second cancers, AML/MDS, and causes of death, including a signal of excess AML/MDS mortality in the CHOP-RIT arm (sHR 3.8)
key_concerns: Imaging follow-up only required for 7 years and no central relapse review, raising residual concern about undercounted late relapses despite sensitivity analyses
No explicit data- or code-availability statement visible; underlying patient-level data and cure-modeling code are not indicated as deposited
Cohort is predominantly non-Hispanic White and half received radioimmunotherapy, a now rarely-used modality, limiting generalizability
Minor typographical error in a reported CI ("31% CI" instead of "95% CI" for high FLIPI cure estimate)
Whether the cure-modeling analysis was pre-specified in the original S0016 protocol or added post hoc is not stated
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically rigorous, clinically paradigm-shifting long-term RCT analysis with state-of-the-art cure modeling and candid limitations; the content is competitive at the top-tier oncology journals, warranting Tier 1 with only minor revisions.
